question.text: This corrupt New York political machine supported many Democratic politicians during the late-19th and early-20th centuries. It was depicted as a ferocious tiger by political cartoonist Thomas Nast.
question.clue: Samuel Tilden investigated a Grand Sachem ("say-chem") of this organization's corrupt namesake "ring."

swap.text: This man had formerly served as the Collector of the Port of New York before being fired. This successor of James Garfield as president signed the Pendleton Civil Service Act into law.
swap.clue: He restructured much of Buchanan's Morrill Tariff with a tariff act labeled the "Mongrel," and accepted a spot on his ticket after the refusal of Levi Morton.

question.leadin: A political cartoon showed this man carried on a chain by his campaign manager Mark Hanna.
question.text: Name this man who defeated William Jennings Bryan in the 1896 presidential election. The Spanish-American War occurred during his presidency, and he was assassinated by Leon Czolgosz in 1901.
question.clue: At the urging of strategist Mark Hanna, he stayed home during a "front porch campaign;" after that campaign succeeded, he dispatched Commodore Dewey to Manila Bay following the explosion of the U.S.S. Maine.

swap.leadin: Eugene Debs was arrested in the aftermath of this event, after which he became a Socialist.
swap.text: Name this railroad strike and boycott that crippled transportation in 1894.
swap.clue: Mediation offers by the local Civic Federation and Mayor John P. Hopkins were turned down, and violence soon broke out at Blue Island.

question.leadin: During the Progressive Era, the federal government attempted to regulate business.
question.text: Standard Oil was broken up into 33 companies when the Supreme Court applied this 1890 antitrust act against it, named after an Ohio Senator.
question.clue: This act was inspired by a similar act from its namesake senator's home state named for Valentine.

swap.leadin: The bending of frame 18 led many to believe that this ship was sunk by a mine, rather than by a fire in its coal bunkers.
swap.text: Name this battleship, whose sinking was investigated years after the fact by Admiral Rickover.
swap.clue: In 1976 Hyman Rickover published a book questioning the long-held belief about the cause of its destruction, claiming that Captain Charles Sigsbee's poor supervision of the coal bunker was the real cause.

question.leadin: The United States government has a sinister history of massacring Native Americans.
question.text: This incident took place on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation in South Dakota. More than 150 men, women, and children from the Lakota Tribe were killed by James Forsyth's 7th Cavalry in this massacre.
question.clue: This event was sparked by the deaf Black Coyote's refusal to hand over his rifle.

swap.leadin: John L. Lewis broke off from it to form the Congress of Industrial Organizations, which later rejoined it.
swap.text: Name this alliance of labor unions aimed at skilled craftsmen that was founded by Samuel Gompers. It was initially opposed to the Knights of Labor.
swap.clue: At its founding in 1886, this organization elected its first president, Samul Gompers.

question.leadin: Allen G. Thurman, a 74-year-old running mate of this man, gave a bizarre speech stating, "I am not quite as well as I ought to be."
question.text: Name this Democrat who lost the 1888 election with Thurman but won four years later against the same opponent with the elder Adlai Stevenson as his running mate.
question.clue: This man used federal troops to put down the Pullman Strike.

swap.text: Henry Frick infamously called in Pinkerton guards in this 1892 strike, leading to a violent clash outside a Carnegie-owned steel plant in a Pennsylvania town.
swap.clue: The leader of the Amalgamated Associations, Hugh O'Donnell, led this strike.

question.leadin: Answer the following about legends of the Wild West.
question.text: The oft-romanticized 1881 gunfight between Wyatt Earp's posse and a group of villainous cowboys is usually named for this building in Tombstone, even though the fight actually took place in a lot adjacent to it.
question.clue: The gunfight at this American location only was about 30 seconds and was between the Cochise County Cowboys and a group of officers that included Doc Holliday.

swap.text: Dee Brown, who participated in the occupation of Alcatraz, wrote a history of the American West titled Bury My Heart at this location. Over 300 Lakota Sioux were killed in a 1890 massacre at this South Dakota location.
swap.answerHtml: Wounded Knee [or Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee]
swap.clue: The Big Foot Memorial Riders end their path at this place, remembering an event that began due to Black Coyote's deafness.

question.leadin: This man brought to light the harsh treatment of miners in Spring Valley, Illinois, but his writings were unable to prevent a large race riot by anarchist Italian miners.
question.text: Name this author of the 1894 expose Wealth Against Commonwealth, in which he criticizes the business practices of monopolies, most notably Standard Oil.

swap.leadin: This religious movement was the subject of a study by anthropologist James Mooney.
swap.text: Name this religious movement begun by Wovoka after seeing a solar eclipse.
swap.clue: That later version was founded by the son of Tavibo, who during a solar eclipse on New Year's Day was taken to the other world and given five songs that would control the weather, as well as invulnerability to weapons.

question.leadin: Learmonth Dalrymple, a prominent member of this organization, pushed to found Otago's first secondary school for girls.
question.text: Name this international organization. A founding member of its New Zealand branch, Kate Sheppard, pushed heavily for Lord Glasgow to pass a law granting women's suffrage in New Zealand.
question.clue: This group, which used the slogan "For God and Home and Every Land" and was led by Annie Wittenmyer, adopted a Xenophon quote to argue for "total abstinence from everything harmful."

swap.text: This group of demands presented in 1890 demanded the free circulation of silver and the abolition of national banks. It is named for the Florida city in which it was given.
swap.clue: The meeting that produced this document took place at the Marion Opera House, and this document takes the form of seven numbered resolutions.

question.leadin: While organizing events hosted by this movement, Keith Vawter helped to popularize entertainers like the Onondaga Indian Concert Band.
question.text: Name this adult education movement, which was named after a lake in Upstate New York. William Jennings Bryan was a popular speaker on this circuit.
question.clue: That and its mobile circuit helped spur membership to more than 260,000 members by the end of the nineteenth century.

swap.text: This organization blamed deaths during the Great Train Wreck of 1918 on shoddy, wooden train cars. This organization was created by an 1887 act to counteract monopolistic railroad practices.
swap.clue: This organization had its power strengthened by the Hepburn and Mann Elkins Act, which regulated "unfair trade practices".

question.leadin: Name these things about a 19th century U.S. election FTPE.
question.text: This presidential election featured the delivery of a speech advocating bimetallism at the Democratic nominating convention in Chicago and the rejection of the pro-business wing of the Democratic party.
question.clue: Thomas Watson repudiated the vice presidential candidacy of Arthur Sewall in this election.

swap.leadin: The only time this political party nominated a candidate who won the presidency was in 1928 when it also nominated the Republican ticket of Hoover and Curtis. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this party that nominated people such as Earl Dodge, John Bidwell and James Black, and supported the passage of the Volstead Act.
swap.clue: The publication of The Hatchet and the activities of the Women's Christian Temperance Union helped generate support for this party, whose goals were briefly realized with the passage of the Volstead Act.
